newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Arafat says he misses Rabin.
newsitem.headline: Arafat says he misses Rabin.

text.p: Palestinian President Yasser Arafat said on Sunday he missed his Israeli peace partner Yitzhak Rabin who was assassinated nearly a year ago by a right-wing Jew.
"His death was a great loss not only for the Palestinians but for the Israelis and the whole area," Arafat told Israel Radio in an interview at his office in self-ruled Gaza.
"Shalom haver (farewell friend)," Arafat addressed the slain prime minister in Hebrew, echoing U.S. President Bill Clinton's simple eulogy delivered moments after Rabin died.
"I miss you," Arafat added in English.
Israel marks the one-year anniversary of Rabin's assassination this week according to the Jewish lunar calendar.

Arafat and Rabin shook hands on the White House lawn in 1993 in a dramatic display of conciliation after decades of Israeli-Palestinian hostilities. The gesture earned the two men Nobel Peace prizes, along with Israel's then foreign minister Shimon Peres.
The handshake paved the way for Palestinian self-rule in parts of the West Bank and Gaza Strip which Israeli troops had occupied since 1967.

A religious Jew gunned Rabin down at a Tel Aviv peace rally last November 4 in a bid to halt implementation of the peace deals. Seven months later right-wing Likud party leader Benjamin Netanyahu ousted Rabin's Labour party in national elections.
Arafat told the radio current U.S.-brokered peace talks with Netanyahu on a long-delayed Israeli withdrawal from the West Bank town of Hebron had achieved no progress.
Chief Israeli and Palestinian negotiators were meeting in Tel Aviv on Sunday ahead of a resumption in formal talks on Monday.
